note: Frozen campaign config of the PAT-19 protocol v4 (PAT-121): the protocol v3 (pat-19-campaign-v3.json, untouched) with changes, two of them meant to remove two suspected defects of the measuring instrument (the plausible, not established, defects named in the v3 results) and the comparison replayed on other terms. Changes: (1) after a judge refusal the corrector receives the names of the failing or erroring hidden tests, at most 20, each with its failure message cut to 300 characters, never a test's source code (the test module and name are visible, and a message can carry a path under the bundle; only the bundle path and the judge's temporary directory are masked), the same text for both arms (correction_feedback; values fixed by the coordinator, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-10-07 before any trial); at most 2 correction rounds (bounds.max_correction_rounds, as v3); (2) every attempt works in a private root, a parent directory that holds nothing but that attempt (isolation.private_attempt_root), the audit of accesses outside the bundle being unchanged; (3) two arms only, A (Sonnet alone) and L (Sonnet with the report of the local explorer), no Haiku arm E: the cloud economy explorer driver is not declared; (4) the local candidate is fixed, qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit, with no new screening (exploration.fixed_candidate: the launcher refuses screen-exploration and any other candidate), same bounds (60 steps, 900 s) and same reload before each task as v3 (exploration.one_task_per_launch); (5) the comparison set is the six tasks of the v3 screening (PR 30, 83, 27, 24, 48, 19; exploration.comparison_task_group 'screening'), already explored by the local explorer during the v3 screening but never played downstream; the exploration is re-run fresh in the comparison; (6) the cap is 80 cloud executions (envelope_recommended). Unchanged: the decision rule (L retained iff acceptance(L) >= acceptance(A) and premium per accepted task (L) <= 0.85 x A, compatibility required; absent data is never zero; insufficient evidence keeps the cloud), the explore prompt, the read-only local explorer driver, the localization ground truth (same file, same sha256), the 10-function cap, the dedicated machine (2 GiB, 35 %), review, the Claude drivers. The values of items (2) to (6) were validated by the maintainer on 2026-10-07; the values of item (1) (20 names, 300 characters per message, 200 characters per name, 2 corrections) are fixed by the coordinator, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-10-07 before any trial. LIMITS: six tasks; tasks already seen by the local explorer in the v3 screening; no Haiku arm; the result says nothing about other task families. A different value of the coordinator-set values means a protocol v5. Changing a coordinate, a bound or a rule opens a protocol v5.

bounds.note: v3 and v4 protocol coordinates (v4 unchanged from v3) (changed from v2: 600 s / 25 steps): explorer_max_seconds 900 (15 min) and explorer_max_steps 60. local_max_seconds and local_max_steps are inherited from v1 and unused in v2, v3 and v4 (no local implementer); cloud_max_seconds and max_correction_rounds are the v1 operational bounds (the implementer arms and the review). There is no cloud explorer in v4 (no arm E). max_correction_rounds 2 is a v4 protocol coordinate.

isolation.note: Launcher choice, not a protocol coordinate, EXCEPT private_attempt_root, which is a protocol v4 coordinate pinned by the loader (see private_attempt_root_note). LOCAL drivers (sandbox-exec): reads under the user's REAL home are denied by default (deny_home_by_default, true), then only the entries of allow_read_home (relative to the home, empty by default) and the root of the harness executable's environment when it lives in the home are allowed back, plus the bundle and the attempt directory (outside the real home in a normal run); the explicit read-deny list below stays on top as a second layer (the last matching rule wins), together with every checkout/worktree of this repository, the state directory and the parent directory of --envelope/--campaign/--snapshot/--manifest (keep them apart from --work-root). Default-deny is unit-tested on the generated profile and was trial-run on 2026-10-05 with the real omp 18.6.1 and mini-swe-agent 2.4.6 (Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit, allow_read_home empty): both passed, so deny_home_by_default stays true (explicit list exercised with the real local harness by PAT-111 as well). The CLOUD drivers run WITHOUT sandbox-exec (sandbox: false with its reason) and NO read denial applies to them: neither deny_home_by_default nor the cloud list below is enforced for them (kept as data for the audit); an unsandboxed cloud arm can read anything the user can (plugin cache, ~/.config, ~/.ssh, repositories), reach the network, and use the user's implicit credentials (git credential helper through the keychain, gh configuration, ~/.config/foundry), and runs without Foundry hooks (--setting-sources project,local: the R1 guard on gh pr merge / git push does not apply). What stands between a cloud arm and the tracker, secrets and merge is: the best-effort cloud_bash_deny rules, the post-run audit of commands and paths (a record whose tool calls ran a forbidden command or touched the plugin cache, another checkout, the user's configuration, the home or an ancestor of the bundle (the attempt directory and, under private_attempt_root, its private parent are allowed; the work root and above are not) is `contaminated`, undecided, cost kept, never replayed), and the fact that the bundle has no remote. The generated profile is itself denied to a sandboxed arm. Not covered: '(allow default)' leaves Mach access to the security daemon, so denying Library/Keychains does not prevent a keychain query.
isolation.private_attempt_root_note: PAT-121: each attempt (implementer, correction, review, exploration) is built in <work-root>/private-<attempt>/<attempt>/, so the parent of the attempt directory contains nothing but that attempt: 'ls ..' from the bundle shows no other attempt. The audit is not weakened: the attempt directory and its private parent are allowed, the work root itself and every other attempt under it are listed among the sensitive roots (a read of another attempt is still a contamination), and every other rule (hidden tests, truth file, ~/.config, other checkouts, forbidden commands) is unchanged. Not set in v1, v2 and v3 (their layout is unchanged).

cloud_bash_deny_note: Best-effort Bash permission rules added to --disallowedTools of the two cloud drivers of v4 (implementer and reviewer) (the loader refuses a real cloud driver whose argv lacks one of them). Claude Code matches a rule against the COMMAND PREFIX: they stop the direct use of the tracker, merge, network and other-agent tools (gh, git push/remote/clone/fetch/pull, curl, wget, claude, codex, omp, ssh, scp, nc, npm, pip install, python -m http, security, open). They are NOT a sandbox: a determined agent evades them (a script, an interpreter one-liner, a renamed binary, an alias, a path-qualified executable, a library call), and the cloud arm keeps the real home, an open network, the user's implicit credentials and bypassPermissions. The post-run audit (command and path audit, contaminated records) detects the direct shapes; it does not prevent anything.

dedicated_machine.note: Protocol v2 admission inherited by v3 and v4 (narrowed system patterns validated by the maintainer on 2026-10-07) (thresholds: maintainer, 2026-10-06; narrowed system patterns: coordinator, 2026-10-07, before any corpus trial; validated by the maintainer on 2026-10-07), applied by the preflight of compare-exploration when arm L runs (screen-exploration is refused in v4; in v2 and v3 it applied before every screening task): refuse when a process outside the allow-list below holds more than max_other_process_rss_gib of resident memory (ps -axo rss=,command=), or when the free memory percentage of memory_pressure is under min_free_percent (35: replaces the 'swap de départ' threshold of the ticket's original AC; swap in use does not come down without a reboot, and the process rule is the real guard, see pat-19-preflight-v2-2026-10-06.json#dedicated_machine_measurement). Both commands are already in the launcher's read-only list. An unreadable output refuses. Only a process NAME (application name or executable basename, never an argument) is recorded with the observed values. The system patterns are deliberately narrow: /System/Library/ (daemons and frameworks), /usr/libexec|sbin|bin, /sbin, /Library/Apple and kernel_task; NOT /System/Applications/ (consumer apps such as Mail or Photos) nor /System/Volumes/Preboot/Cryptexes/App/ (Safari/WebKit), which are ordinary memory consumers.

exploration.note: Report format of the explorers: one JSON object {"files": [repo-relative paths], "functions": [{"file", "name"}], "rationale": str}; all three keys required. Read from <scratch>/report.json when the arm wrote one, else from the final message of its stream. A missing or unusable report, an exploration cut by a bound (time or steps) or a bundle whose git status changed is a refusal (score 0), never a void attempt. Only the FIRST 10 functions of a report count for function recall and are passed to the implementer of arm L (report_render_limits.max_functions must stay 10).

ground_truth.note: the single source of the ground truth: the launcher loads this committed file and refuses (campaign load, code 2, before any attempt) a file whose sha256 differs

protocol_coordinates.note: These determine the score or the verdicts of the comparison and are stated in the protocol (sections 3 to 5 of the protocol v4 and the inherited sections of v3 and v2): they ARE protocol coordinates; changing one opens a protocol v5.

function_cap.rationale: only the first 10 functions of a report count for function recall and reach the implementer of arm L (report_render_limits.max_functions must equal it)

protocol_coordinates.function_name_match: a reported function name matches a true function in the same file when it equals the qualified name or its last component
protocol_coordinates.empty_report_precision: a valid report with no file has file precision 0 (undefined ratio counted as 0, so the precision floor cannot be met by saying nothing)
protocol_coordinates.localization_ground_truth: recall uses the product files and functions only (the judge's own classification: SOURCE_PREFIXES, not tests, not documentation); precision counts a reported file as correct when the merged diff really changed or created it, product or not; files the diff adds are not counted in recall and functions that do not exist at the base SHA are not counted in function recall: an explorer cannot find what does not exist yet. A removed line is read in the base source, an added line in the merged source; the diff algorithm is pinned (myers)
protocol_coordinates.premium_work_definition: premium work = unweighted sum of the four billing token classes (input, cached input, cache write, output) over ALL models, explorer included: a Haiku explorer counts as premium, local tokens do not; a limit: an economy model's token weighs the same as a premium one, hence the per-model breakdown in the report
protocol_coordinates.refused_report_in_comparison: when an explorer of the comparison yields no usable report, its implementer runs on the plain statement and the explorer's cost stays counted (the end-to-end cost of using the explorer); a contaminated or twice-cut explorer leaves the arm undecided for that task
protocol_coordinates.quality_bounds_on_undecided: quality compares acceptance counts with undecided tasks as bounds: pass only if it holds in the worst case, fail only if it fails in the best case, else unavailable
protocol_coordinates.economy_unavailable_cases: premium per accepted task is unavailable (never zero) when a compared task is undecided, spent work is unknown, a premium total is unknown or an arm accepted no task

exploration.one_task_per_launch_note: Protocol v3 reload rule, inherited by v4 (written in advance): the launcher loads no model, so with this flag screen-exploration (refused in v4) plays at most ONE not-yet-decided task of the candidate per launch and compare-exploration at most ONE comparison task (all its requested arms) per launch, then exits 0 and prints 'pat19-v3: work_remains=yes' or 'pat19-v3: work_remains=no' on stdout. The operator unloads and reloads the pinned model between launches (pat-19-v3-operator.md). Resume semantics are unchanged (a decided task is skipped). The per-task reload is attested by the operator script plus one session (one ledger preflight) per task, not by the launcher. Same rule in v4 (the line printed is unchanged: pat19-v3: work_remains=...).
exploration.v4_note: PAT-121: the comparison runs on the six tasks of the v3 screening (manifest group 'screening': PR 30, 83, 27, 24, 48, 19), recorded under the task set 'comparison' (the records keep their v2 shape). They were explored locally during the v3 screening but never played downstream. The candidate is fixed by the protocol (no screening results are needed; screen-exploration is refused). The ground truth file covers these tasks (same file and sha256 as v2 and v3).

min_free_disk_gib.rationale: launcher safety margin for model files and bundles; the protocol states no disk threshold

swap_metric.rationale: extra swap is measured as the maximum, over local attempts, of (swap after - swap before); the protocol does not define how to measure it

explorer_tool_names.rationale: the read-only tool set of the local explorer is --tools=read,grep,glob. The maintainer validated the read-only intent on 2026-10-06 as read,grep,find,ls; the toy trial of omp 18.6.1 refused it ("Unknown tool in --tools: ls"; find is "unavailable in this session"; the built-ins include read, grep, glob), so the names were corrected to the same trio as the cloud explorer (Read/Grep/Glob) before the freeze. The loader accepts only read, grep, glob.

report_source_and_prompt.rationale: the pinned tool sets have no file-writing tool, so the prompt asks for the JSON as the final message and the launcher reads it from the stream; an arm-written <scratch>/report.json is also accepted. The shapes of the final messages were pinned by the real toy trials of 2026-10-06 and, with the frozen prompt, of 2026-10-07 (pat-19-preflight-v2-2026-10-06.json: drivers, final_prompt_trial)

report_render_limits.rationale: a report appended to a statement is cut at 20 files and 1500 rationale characters, with a visible note; the scoring is not affected. The cap of 10 functions is a protocol coordinate (exploration.protocol_coordinates.function_cap)

envelope_recommendation.rationale: the caps below are a recommendation for the operator's envelope file (the launcher never writes one); the envelope stays the operator's

explorer_bundle_unchanged_check.rationale: the launcher records git status --porcelain of the bundle before and after each exploration (local and cloud); a modified or unreadable bundle refuses the exploration (score 0, never replayed). Kept in v4 for the local explorer (no cloud explorer is declared); in v2/v3 it was needed because the cloud explorer is not sandboxed (Bash open): read-only behaviour is observed, not enforced

statement_footer:
---
Launcher note (identical for every arm): work only inside this repository. Do not create virtual environments, install packages or create node_modules in the tree; use the interpreter already on PATH. Do not create or edit test configuration files (conftest.py, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, tox.ini, setup.cfg, sitecustomize.py, *.pth).

prompts.implement: Implement the task described in {statement_file}. Work only inside the current repository: change the product code and add tests if useful. Run the relevant tests, then stop when you consider the task done.
prompts.correct: The task is described in {statement_file}. A previous attempt is already applied in this repository. Apply the corrections listed in {feedback_file}, run the relevant tests, then stop.
prompts.review: Independently review the uncommitted change in this repository (git diff HEAD) against the task in {statement_file}. Do not modify any file. Write {review_file} as JSON: {"verdict": "PASS" or "BLOCK", "findings": ["..."]}.
prompts.explore: Prepare the task described in {statement_file} by exploring this repository READ-ONLY: do not modify any file, do not run tests, do not write anything. You have at most {max_duration} (and at most {max_steps} tool steps where the harness counts them): answer with the JSON BEFORE reaching them, an exploration cut by a bound is refused and scores 0. Find where the change must be made. Your final message must be exactly one JSON object and nothing else: {"files": ["repo-relative path", ...], "functions": [{"file": "repo-relative path", "name": "function or Class.method"}], "rationale": "short explanation"}. List the files and the functions that need to change, not the ones you merely read; at most 10 functions, most relevant first (only the first 10 count).

exploration_screening.note: Not played in v4 (the candidate is fixed, exploration.fixed_candidate; screen-exploration is refused). Kept so that the v2 schema is satisfied and so that the v3 rule stays readable: MAIN metric = mean FUNCTION recall over the 6 tasks (maintainer decision 2026-10-06, before the freeze: each task's truth is a single product file and 5 of the 6 screening tasks share linear.py, so file recall is near-trivial). Candidates were the two frozen ones of v3 (in v4 the candidates list holds only qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit, fixed) and the v3 screening was complete only when both had their 6 tasks decided. Eligible = mean file precision >= 0.5; the best mean function recall is compared to retained_function_recall_min BEFORE any tie (below 0.5: STOP 'conserver le cloud', also for a tie; exactly 0.5 is retained); then a tie goes to the shortest total duration, and a tie still unresolved to the candidate listed first in candidates. STOP also when no candidate has mean file precision >= 0.5. File recall is measured and reported but does not decide. A task whose truth has no function (none today) is excluded from the function-recall mean. A refused or contaminated attempt counts 0 on every metric and never blocks the screening: an assumed departure from 'absent data is never zero', limited to this filter (the comparison keeps unknown as unknown). Inherited from v2 and v3; kept readable, not applied in v4.

exploration_comparison.note: arm L is retained only if compatibility AND quality AND economy all pass on the 6 tasks: its acceptance rate >= A's AND its premium tokens per accepted task (explorer included; a Haiku explorer counts as premium, local tokens do not) <= 0.85 x A's, and compatibility (the v1 machine criterion: no external signal, extra swap under extra_swap_gib_max) passes. v4 has no arm E. Local wall time is reported; no time ratio is part of the v2 rule. Rule unchanged from v2 and v3; v4 runs it on the six tasks of the v3 screening.

compare_exploration.justification: Per task and arm at most 1 implementer + 2 corrections and 3 reviews = 6 executions: 2 arms x 6 tasks x 6 = 72 <= 80 (no Haiku exploration in v4; the cap holds the worst case, the minimum is 24). premium_tokens 40 000 000 is 500 000 per execution of 80, the per-execution allowance of v3 (a cap stops the campaign, it is not an estimate). wall_clock 100 000 s (27.8 h) as in v3: it covers 72 cloud executions at ~10 min plus 6 x 900 s of local exploration.

local_explorer.note: Protocol v2 read-only local explorer: omp 18.6.1 as the v1 local_harness plus --tools=read,grep,glob (no edit, write or bash tool), the bundle READ-ONLY in the sandbox profile (only the attempt scratch writable), bounded by explorer_max_seconds/steps. Trial-run on 2026-10-06 (see evidence): with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MLX 4-bit, sandbox on, bundle read-only, deny-home: exit 0, 14.0 s, 4 steps, bundle unchanged, final-message report parsed. The first argv (--tools=read,grep,find,ls) was refused by omp.

session_log.layout_note: Verified on 2026-10-05 (PAT-111): the launcher's reading of <projects_dir>/*/<session>.jsonl equals the host's own result.usage exactly for the three drivers, one file per session id. Conditional on the launcher's assertion, from the stream's system/init event, that the arm's tools are a subset of allowed_tools (Bash, Edit, Read, Write; so no sub-agent, workflow, web or scheduling tool): a record whose init event lists any other tool, or has none, is refused (tool_error).

cloud_implementer_current.note: Claude Code 2.1.285 headless, current routed implementer profile (Sonnet 5.5, effort medium). The first 2026-10-05 trial ran with `--disallowedTools Agent` only; the FINAL argv (29 tool names + the cloud_bash_deny rules) was then trial-run on the toy task on 2026-10-05 (init: exactly Bash, Edit, Read, Write) and passed, see the evidence. Bare Claude Code with the protocol's model and effort: no Foundry plugin, hook, agent definition (not the Eiffel or Maigret definitions), --permission-mode bypassPermissions, tools restricted to Read/Edit/Write/Bash with Bash otherwise unrestricted except for the best-effort deny rules.
cloud_implementer_current.sandbox_reason: Claude Code cannot authenticate under sandbox-exec ('Not logged in' with the keychain denied, '401 OAuth access token has been revoked' with it allowed; cause not established). The arm runs unsandboxed with the AGENTS.md R6 environment intact (real HOME, LANG, LC_ALL, LOGNAME, PATH, TMPDIR, USER) in the disposable bundle; its tool calls are audited after the run. Consequences, not mitigated by the launcher: real home, open network, the user's implicit credentials, no Foundry hook (no R1 guard); see cloud_bash_deny and isolation.note.

qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit.generation_parameters: server and harness defaults, not overridden by the launcher (no temperature, top_p, top_k, seed or max_tokens is passed)

candidates_note: model = the LM Studio model key, which is also the identifier the operator gives at load (lms load <key> -c 65536 --identifier <key> --parallel 1) and the name the harness sends; the HF repo of the protocol is kept as hf_repo_provenance. The operator loads, the launcher loads nothing. The preflight reads the loaded instance (lms ps --json) and refuses when its model key differs, its quantization differs or its context length is below min_context (65536, a frozen coordinate: LM Studio ignored -c for some MLX builds). File digests, chat-template digest and generation parameters are recorded here and in pat-19-preflight-2026-10-05.json; they are not recomputed by the launcher. Generation parameters are the server and harness defaults, not overridden. Protocol v4 keeps only qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mlx-4bit, unchanged (qwen3-coder is not compared: no new screening).

correction_feedback.note: PAT-121 (values fixed by the coordinator, confirmed by the maintainer on 2026-10-07 before any trial: max_failures 20, max_message_chars 300, max_name_chars 200, and the 2 correction rounds of bounds). After a judge REFUSED verdict the corrector's feedback file adds the failing or erroring hidden tests (junit classname::name cut to max_name_chars, a parametrized id can carry test data), at most max_failures of them, each with the junit failure message cut to max_message_chars characters (whitespace collapsed, the candidate's location replaced by <bundle>, the judge's temporary directory by <tmp>), and the line 'N shown of M' (the count not shown is M - N). Never the test source code (the test module and name are visible, and a message can carry a path under the bundle; only the bundle path and the judge's temporary directory are masked); but the pytest message can carry the expression of an assertion and the expected values, so a corrector can fit code to the tests (the same for both arms). A collection error only yields a collection-failure message: the feedback then teaches nothing (its share in v3 is unknown). A refusal with no test list (timeout, harness files changed, candidate fault) adds nothing. Identical for arms A and L (same code path). Absent from the v1, v2 and v3 configs, where the key is refused at load: their feedback is unchanged. Each correction record carries counters only (feedback: failing_shown, failing_total, collection_failure), never text.
